cells.tense: The checking runs in the same moment the speaking does, and both are here.
cells.ask: With someone you trust, answer one direct question with the plain version instead of the one that keeps every door open. Notice which one you were about to send.
cells.core:
You can say the true thing without lighting a fire with it. You hear how something will land and you still say it, and the care is in the timing rather than in the softening. People bring you the version of events they can't make sense of, and you hand it back straighter without making them smaller.

That other thing, the pull toward what you actually want — it doesn't stall the way it used to. You're not spending the whole week proving the direction is sensible, going back over the choice until it feels safe enough to act on. The message sent actually says what it means, and it gets less correcting afterward, not more.
cells.sheetLine: You say the true thing and it lands, because you checked it first.
cells.verb: speaking true things plainly, checked against what the moment can hold
cells.place: the place where what you want is what you steer by

cells.tense: Some future room is being prepared for a conversation that has not happened yet.
cells.ask: Send one small correction now, in the plain words you'd use if nobody were listening. Then let that version stand without a follow-up.
cells.core:
Done cleanly, this is quick: you say the thing, the other person takes it in, the conversation moves on. One correction, and then it's over. You get one step clear and take it, and the next thing gets decided while you're actually in it.

What's happening instead is the conversation getting rehearsed rather than had. Every version of what you might say is tested against the one you might want in some later room, so you get clear about everything except the next step. People feel it in how you talk: a question gets answered before it's finished, a small thing gets corrected before it matters. Before you've lived the morning, you've already decided how the afternoon goes.
cells.sheetLine: You've checked it so far ahead that nothing has happened yet.

cells.tense: The moment for saying it plainly came and went, and you're still standing there.
cells.ask: Say one piece of what you know to one person this week, in whatever words come out. Let it be rough.
cells.core:
You have things worth putting into words and you keep them in. Saying something plainly has been followed by silence before, so the checking goes quiet now instead of loud — what comes out is softer, more agreeable, less true. What you want is out there somewhere and you're waiting for a pull strong enough to move you before you say a word about it.

Seeing straight isn't the trouble. You've got plenty of that. It's the part where the true thing leaves your mouth and meets another person, and you find out it's survivable. Somewhere along the line that stopped feeling possible, so what you know sits there, ready and unused.
cells.sheetLine: You've gone quiet with what you know, and it shows.

cells.tense: You're already steering by a clear read of the room and not counting it as steering.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you decided this week, on your own, that nobody noticed you deciding. Say it out loud to one person.
cells.core:
You keep finding the true version of a story without noticing you're the one finding it. Somebody's confused about what happened; somewhere in the back of the conversation, the thing gets set straight, and you'd call it just saying what's obvious. Whatever half-said thing you're carrying around and doing nothing about — that's the pull, unnamed, and it doesn't get counted either.

The straightening runs through you all day. You're the one who keeps the details honest, and you'd rather it were the details doing it. Naming it changes nothing about the room, except who gets credit for keeping it straight.

attempts.check: The record gives the card's behavior (calibration, truth spoken with care) and the seat (the pull toward what's genuinely wanted), but nothing about this person's habits, history, or what they are actually doing — so each cell describes the mechanism in a moment, never a biography. A reader could object that the card's parent archetype leans on the Analyst role and its bounds, which sit past what the seat alone shows, so I keep to what the person could recognize: a self-check that fires, and where it fires on the desire. The ask survives a wrong read in every status because it is one visible act — an answer given plainly, a small correction sent, one honest sentence, a piece of knowledge handed to one person — useful regardless of which seat is running. The sentence that serves the writer more than them would be any line that casts them as a teacher of others or a keeper of clear perception; that flatters the card and never reaches the person. I also dropped the temptation to say what a past door in the Too Little cell was; the cell may locate the person behind the room without saying what happened there.
